name: 0046 block 2 - linear 24 V PSU 30 min
description: BLOCK 2. Identical to block 0 except the sensor supply is the LINEAR 24 VDC lab supply instead of the switch-mode one. The delta against block 0 IS the switch-mode PSU's own contribution, isolated. If noise drops here, the switch-mode supply is a culprit. THIS PROFILE DOES NOT TOUCH THE DRIVE. The rpm schedule is deliberately empty and vfd_stop_on_end is false, so the runner never sends a frequency, never starts and never stops the motor -- the operator is in control of the drive by hand. It only acquires, for the stated duration, and logs telemetry. Ticket 0046 electrical-noise characterization. Same acquisition and scope_channels as a normal run, so blocks compare without rescaling. Heater relay must be OFF for every electrical block (it is its own EMI source, ticket 0035) -- it only comes back as its own factor in block 6. RUNNER NOTE — WHY max_consecutive_modbus_errors IS DISABLED HERE: this block requires the VFD powered down at the mains, and the runner polls vfd.get_status() every tick for logging. With the drive dead those reads time out, the failed connects leave the shared RS485 port locked so the Omron read fails too, and the runner's safety stop fires at 10 consecutive errors — it killed the first attempt at this block 3 minutes in (stop_reason=modbus_errors>=10, 2026-09-30). That safety stop exists so a run does not continue blind after comms die, which is right for a real run and meaningless here: the motor is off, we never command it, and this block needs nothing but the scope. So it is raised for THIS profile only. DO NOT copy this setting into a profile that drives the motor — there it is the thing that stops a run whose drive has stopped answering. Expect the log to fill with 'Could not exclusively lock port /dev/ttyUSB0' and omron_pv_c to be null; both are expected here.
